title: Too Much / Not Enough
description: Explain why an amount or quality does not fit a need.
objectives: Explain why an amount or quality does not fit a need.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to explain why an amount or quality does not fit a need. The central language is too much/many and not enough. It belongs to the practical context of comparing & choosing. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the too much / not enough exchange.

blocks.english: There aren't enough seats for everyone.
blocks.explanation: This too much / not enough model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the too much / not enough exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “This bag costs too much.” and “There aren't enough seats for everyone.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: too much/many and not enough.

There aren't enough seats for everyone. Which option do you prefer?
